about: Settings for FACTUAL CORRECTNESS (task-success dimension) on the held-out questions. RAGAS does the judging with its own built-in prompts, unchanged; this file only records the choices RAGAS cannot make for us: the reference answer, the mode, how finely to split claims, what counts as the answer, and the judge. LOCK RULE: never change this file after its results are seen; make a new version instead.
metric_question: Did the facts the operator needed make it into the final answer?
why_recall: Our reference is a short list of facts the answer MUST contain, not everything it is allowed to say. Precision would punish true, useful extra detail that simply isn't on the list. Made-up content is already measured by faithfulness. Recall also closes the funnel on the grounding card: needed -> found -> kept -> reached the writer -> in the answer (the 'answer completeness' step marked 'not measured yet').

reference.from: retrieval_labels.json (locked 2026-11-15, fingerprint checked at run time)
reference.means: For each case, every needed fact's 'fact' text, one sentence per fact, joined into one reference text. All 50 facts (H1 7, H2 11, H3 11, H4 11, H5 10).
reference.note_h1: H1's facts were written after its answer had been read (not blind; recorded in retrieval_labels.json). H1 is reported, but marked not blind.

response_means: The final report as graded, without the REPORT CONFIDENCE and SOURCE DATA blocks, and with 'Step N:' labels removed (the actions stay). Same answer text as faithfulness v2, so the two metrics judge the same thing.

evaluator.prompts: RAGAS built-in claim-splitting and claim-checking prompts, unchanged
evaluator.steps_used: Only the reference -> answer direction, with RAGAS's own steps unchanged: split the reference into claims (ClaimDecompositionPrompt) and check each claim against the answer (NLIStatementPrompt). The score is then computed by our rule below, not by RAGAS's combined formula.
evaluator.why_not_ragas_score: Found in the RAGAS 0.4.3 source before locking: its 'recall' = TP / (TP + FN), where TP counts ANSWER claims backed by the reference and FN counts REFERENCE claims missing from the answer. It mixes two directions, so a long answer repeating one fact many times scores higher. Our rule counts reference claims only. This also skips splitting the long report (fewer tokens).

settings_explained.mode recall: Of the reference claims, how many does the answer support? Extra claims in the answer are not counted.
settings_explained.atomicity high: Split into the smallest single facts, to match the size of our locked facts ('weigh 20 bottles' and '495-505 ml' become two claims).
settings_explained.coverage high: Keep every detail and number in each claim, so a vague answer ('weigh some bottles') gets no credit for a precise fact ('weigh the first 20 bottles').

rules.split: RAGAS splits the reference into claims (atomicity high, coverage high)
rules.verdict: For each reference claim, the judge decides whether the answer supports it (1) or not (0)
rules.score: reference claims supported by the answer / all reference claims

first_run_check.about: Run ONE case first (H2) and have a person check, before running the others: (1) did RAGAS split our facts sensibly (no fact lost, no claim invented, numbers kept)? (2) is each 1/0 verdict right? If the splitting is wrong, stop and make version 2; do not tune and re-run silently.

also_report.per_fact: Map each reference claim back to its fact id (by code: the fact sharing the most words with the claim; a person confirms on the first run) so a missed fact can be compared with the grounding funnel (never found / dropped by a helper / reached the writer but left out of the answer).
also_report.wrong_value: Manual review of every MISSING fact: if the answer states the same thing with a DIFFERENT value (for example 1.4 bar where the SOP says 1.3), label it WRONG, not just missing. A wrong value is worse than a missing one. Quote the answer text.

manual_review_rule: A claim counts as present only with the same meaning and the same numbers; a vaguer statement does not count (same rule as the handover recall review). Corrections are recorded as data, pointing to the review, never by editing results.
known_limits: An AI judge decides each verdict; a person checks the first run and every MISSING fact.
Recall does not punish made-up content; faithfulness measures that.
The reference is only the facts we listed as needed; a needed fact we forgot to list is invisible to this metric.
